intro.title: Build lazy module loader for route chunks
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a lazy module loader that dynamically imports JavaScript code for different route chunks in a web application. You'll learn the core concept of code-splitting, which improves performance by loading only the necessary parts of an app when needed. The main technologies involved are JavaScript's dynamic `import()` function and the `Promise` API for handling asynchronous operations. By the end, you'll create a function that loads a module on-demand and returns it for use in your routes, making your app faster and more efficient.
intro.usecase: Lazy loading route chunks is essential in modern web applications where performance matters. You'll see this pattern in large-scale dashboards like analytics platforms or e-commerce admin panels, where different sections (reports, inventory, user management) load only when needed. This approach is also used in complex forms with multiple steps, where each step's validation logic and UI components load dynamically. By implementing lazy module loading, you ensure faster initial page loads and better user experience, especially for users on slower connections or mobile devices.
